groups.title: General (all models)
groups.intro: Habits that improve results no matter which model you use.

tips.title: Build prompts in a fixed order
tips.body: Start with the subject, then what it is doing, the setting, composition, lighting, camera or medium, and finally style. Most models give more weight to what comes first, so lead with what matters most.
tips.example: A weathered fisherman mending a net on a wooden pier, low morning sun, medium shot, 50mm lens, shallow depth of field, muted film colors
do: Name one clear subject first
Add lighting and framing on purpose
avoid: Burying the subject after long style lists
Mixing clashing styles (e.g. photo and watercolor) in one prompt

tips.title: Match prompt style to the model
tips.body: Older CLIP-based models (SD 1.5, SDXL anime finetunes) respond best to short comma-separated keywords or tags. Newer models with large language encoders (FLUX, Qwen-Image, Z-Image, Chroma, Krea 2) understand full sentences and do better with descriptive prose.
do: Tags for SD 1.5, Pony, Illustrious
Sentences for FLUX, Qwen-Image, Z-Image, Krea 2, Chroma

tips.title: Same prompt, different models
tips.body: Each model reads the same words its own way: framing, light, style and how literally it takes the prompt differ a lot. The row shows one prompt and seed on five model types, each at its own recommended steps and guidance. The older SD 1.5 takes the cat apart, SDXL Turbo goes close, the newer models with language encoders build the whole scene.
do: Use each model's own recommended settings when comparing
avoid: Judging a model by settings made for another one

tips.title: Use weighting sparingly
tips.body: In SD-style syntax, (word) boosts a term by about 1.1x and (word:1.3) sets an explicit weight. Small nudges between about 0.8 and 1.4 are usually enough; large weights break the image. Models with language encoders follow plain wording closely and often gain little from weights.
tips.example: portrait of a woman, (freckles:1.2), soft window light
avoid: Weights above about 1.5
Stacking many nested parentheses

tips.title: Know when negative prompts work
tips.body: Negative prompts only take effect when the model runs with real classifier-free guidance (guidance above 1). SD 1.5, SDXL, SD 3.5, Chroma, Qwen-Image, Z-Image Base and Wan use them; distilled models such as FLUX.1, distilled FLUX.2 klein and Z-Image Turbo ignore them.
do: Keep negatives short and specific (blurry, watermark, extra fingers)
avoid: Huge copied negative lists; they can flatten the image

tips.title: Lock the seed to compare changes
tips.body: The seed fixes the starting noise. Keep it constant while you change one word or setting at a time so you can see what that change did; switch to random seeds to explore new compositions.
do: Change one thing per run
Note the seeds of images you like

tips.title: Every seed is a new picture
tips.body: The seed is the starting noise. With the same prompt and settings, every seed gives a different composition: where the cat lies, where the window is, what the light does. The row shows SDXL Turbo with one prompt and four seeds. Find a composition you like by trying seeds, then keep that seed while you refine the prompt.
do: Try several seeds before rewriting the prompt
Keep the seed of a picture you like

tips.title: Steps and guidance basics
tips.body: More steps add refinement up to a point, then only cost time. Guidance (CFG) sets how strictly the prompt is followed: too high gives harsh contrast, oversaturation and artifacts, too low gives vague results. Distilled turbo models need very few steps and little or no guidance.
do: Start from the model's recommended defaults
Lower guidance if colors look burnt
avoid: Running a 4-step turbo model at 50 steps or high CFG

tips.title: Guidance from low to high
tips.body: Guidance sets how hard the model pushes towards the prompt. Too low gives soft, washed-out pictures; around the model's default it looks natural; higher makes colours harsh and adds artifacts; very high burns the picture. The row shows SD 1.5 with one prompt and seed at guidance 1.5, 4, 7, 12 and 20.
do: Start at the model's default and move in small steps
avoid: Very high guidance to force the prompt

tips.title: Steps: refinement up to a point
tips.body: Steps are how often the model refines the picture. Too few leave it unfinished and noisy; at the model's usual count it is clean; beyond that it barely changes and only costs time. The row shows SD 1.5 with one prompt and seed at 5, 10, 20 and 40 steps.
avoid: Many more steps than the model needs: it only costs time

tips.title: Generate at the model's native size
tips.body: Each model is trained around a pixel budget: about 512 px for SD 1.5, about 1 megapixel (1024x1024) for SDXL, SD 3.5 and FLUX, and more for some newer models. Change the aspect ratio but keep the total pixel count similar; much larger sizes cause duplicated subjects and odd anatomy.
do: Portrait ratios for people, wide ratios for landscapes
Upscale afterwards for large prints

tips.title: Iterate: img2img, inpaint, upscale
tips.body: Get the composition right first, then fix details. Use img2img at moderate strength to vary an image you like, inpaint small regions (a hand, a face, a sign) with a focused prompt, and finish with an upscaler or a low-strength high-resolution pass.
do: Strength around 0.3-0.5 for subtle fixes
Inpaint one problem at a time
avoid: Regenerating a whole image to fix one hand

groups.title: Anatomy and people
groups.intro: How to get believable faces, hands and poses for adult subjects.

tips.title: Describe people concretely
tips.body: Give age range, build, hair, clothing and expression instead of vague words like beautiful. Concrete details steer the model toward a specific, natural-looking adult.
tips.example: A man in his forties with a short grey beard, navy wool coat and a calm half-smile, standing by a rainy window

tips.title: Frame hands so they read clearly
tips.body: Hands work best when they are visible, not overlapping, and doing a simple action like holding a cup. Interlocked fingers and complex gestures fail most often, especially on SD 1.5 and SDXL.
do: Give hands a simple task (holding, resting on a table)
Use a larger image so hands get more pixels
avoid: Interlaced fingers and complex gestures in small images

images.caption: Short prompt
images.prompt: a woman holding a cup

images.caption: Detailed prompt
images.prompt: close-up of an adult woman's hands holding a ceramic cup with both hands, five relaxed fingers on each hand, natural nails, soft window light, shallow depth of field

tips.title: Fix faces and hands with inpainting
tips.body: Mask the broken area and regenerate it with a short prompt for just that part. Moderate strength (roughly 0.35-0.5) keeps lighting consistent with the rest of the image; higher values can look pasted in. In VulKara, paint over the part on the Inpaint page and describe just that part.
do: Fix one hand at a time
Reuse the style words of the original prompt

tips.title: Give small faces more pixels
tips.body: Faces in wide or full-body shots get few pixels and come out mushy. Frame closer, use a higher resolution, or run a face detail pass afterwards.
do: Use portrait aspect ratios for full-body shots

tips.title: Control poses with references
tips.body: When a pose matters, a pose reference (an OpenPose-style ControlNet or a model's reference-image input) is far more reliable than describing joint angles in words.
do: Use a clear photo or pose skeleton as guide
avoid: Long text descriptions of limb positions

tips.title: How a pose picture steers the result
tips.body: A pose picture (a skeleton from the Pose page) fixes where head, arms and legs go; the prompt still decides who, what they wear and the light. Without it the model picks a pose of its own; at weight 0.5 the pose is largely taken over, at 1 it is followed closely, down to the bent leg. The row shows one prompt and seed without a pose and with the pose at two weights (SDXL with a pose ControlNet).
do: Match the picture's proportions to the pose picture
Describe clothes and setting in the prompt
avoid: Poses the prompt contradicts (e.g. sitting in the prompt, standing in the pose)

images.prompt: full body photo of a dancer in a flowing red dress on a theatre stage, warm spotlight, dark background

tips.title: Keep multiple people distinct
tips.body: Models tend to blend attributes between people. Describe each person in their own clause with a position (left, right, foreground) and keep the count small; language-encoder models handle this much better than SD 1.5.
tips.example: On the left, a tall woman in a red raincoat; on the right, a shorter man in a green sweater, both laughing at a bus stop

tips.title: Eyes: describe gaze and light
tips.body: Saying where the person looks (at the camera, out of the window) plus a soft light source tends to give aligned eyes with clean catchlights. Mismatched eyes are a typical quick inpainting fix.

images.prompt: an eye

images.caption: Detailed prompt
images.prompt: macro photo of a human eye, detailed iris with fine radial fibers, a small window reflection in the pupil, individual eyelashes, sharp focus, soft daylight

groups.title: Details and quality
groups.intro: Words and settings that add texture and avoid the plastic AI look.

tips.title: Name materials and surfaces
tips.body: Specific materials give the model something concrete to render: brushed aluminum, worn leather, linen, wet asphalt, rough plaster. Generic words like detailed add little.
tips.example: close-up of a ceramic mug with a matte speckled glaze on an oak table, steam rising

images.caption: Short prompt
images.prompt: a teapot

images.caption: Detailed prompt
images.prompt: a hand-thrown stoneware teapot with a speckled matte glaze and a small chip at the rim, on a weathered oak table, low side light from a window, still life photo

tips.title: Describe hair as strands and light
tips.body: Hair looks real when the prompt names its texture and how light falls on it: strands, waves or curls, flyaway hairs, and a backlight or rim light that makes them glow. Just a colour gives a smooth helmet of hair.
do: Name the texture (wavy, coarse, fine, braided)
Add backlight or rim light
avoid: Only a hair colour

images.caption: Short prompt
images.prompt: a woman with red hair

images.caption: Detailed prompt
images.prompt: back view of a woman with long wavy auburn hair, individual strands and a few flyaway hairs catching warm backlight, soft rim light, dark background

tips.title: Use real lighting language
tips.body: Describe the light source, direction and quality: golden-hour backlight, soft overcast light, hard noon sun, rim light, neon reflections, candlelight. Lighting is one of the strongest levers for mood and realism.
do: Name a light source and direction
avoid: Leaving lighting unspecified (often looks flat)

images.caption: Short prompt
images.prompt: a street at night

images.caption: Detailed prompt
images.prompt: a narrow wet cobblestone street at night, warm sodium street lamps, reflections in the puddles, light fog, cinematic, 35mm photo

tips.title: Avoid the over-smoothed plastic look
tips.body: Very high guidance, beauty words and stacked quality tags tend to give waxy skin. Lower guidance a little and ask for natural imperfections such as skin texture, pores, fine wrinkles or film grain.
do: Mention natural skin texture or film grain
Try slightly lower guidance
avoid: Piling up flawless, perfect skin, 8k, masterpiece

images.caption: Short prompt
images.prompt: portrait of an old man

images.caption: Detailed prompt
images.prompt: photo of an old fisherman, weathered skin with visible pores and fine wrinkles, grey stubble, natural overcast light, 85mm lens, no retouching

tips.title: Use camera and film terms for photos
tips.body: Lens length, aperture and film or camera type steer realism: 35mm street photo, 85mm f/1.8 portrait, analog film, flash snapshot. Modern models respond well to these cues.
tips.example: candid 35mm film photo of a busy night market, tungsten light, slight grain

tips.title: Prevent unwanted text artifacts
tips.body: Older models often add scribbles, watermarks or fake signatures. Add watermark, text, signature to the negative prompt where supported; on models without negatives, describe a clean, unbranded surface.
do: Negative for SD and SDXL: watermark, text, logo, signature

tips.title: Put wanted text in quotes
tips.body: Models with good text rendering (FLUX, Qwen-Image, Z-Image, Ideogram 4, SD 3.5) do best when the exact words are in quotation marks, kept short, with placement and style described. SD 1.5 and most SDXL models cannot spell reliably.
tips.example: a vintage enamel shop sign that reads "OPEN LATE" in bold cream letters on dark green
avoid: Whole paragraphs of text in one image

tips.title: Add detail with a second pass
tips.body: For fine detail, generate at native size and then upscale, optionally with a low-strength img2img pass, instead of generating huge images directly.

groups.title: Working with LoRAs
groups.intro: LoRAs add styles, characters or concepts on top of a base model.

tips.title: Match the LoRA to the base family
tips.body: A LoRA only works with the model family it was trained for: SD 1.5, SDXL (Pony and Illustrious often need their own), FLUX.1, FLUX.2, Qwen-Image, Z-Image and so on. The download page lists the base model.
avoid: Loading an SDXL LoRA on SD 1.5 or FLUX

tips.title: Use the trigger words
tips.body: Many LoRAs only activate when their trigger word or phrase is in the prompt. Copy it from the LoRA's page and place it near the start.
do: Look for trigger or activation words on the LoRA page

tips.title: Start around 0.6-0.8 weight
tips.body: Weight 1.0 is the trained strength, but many LoRAs look best somewhere between about 0.5 and 0.9. Raise it if the effect is too weak, lower it if the image distorts or ignores your prompt.
do: Adjust in steps of about 0.1

tips.title: How the weight changes the picture
tips.body: The weight sets how strongly a LoRA pulls the picture towards what it learned. Low weights add a touch of its style while the base model still decides; around 1 the LoRA takes over; well above 1 it starts to break the picture (blocky, noisy or burnt). The row shows one prompt and seed without the LoRA and with a pixel-art LoRA at rising weights (Z-Image Turbo); at 1.5 the picture falls apart. VulKara puts a LoRA's trigger words in front of the prompt when they are missing.
do: Raise the weight in steps of 0.1-0.2
Look at the LoRA's page for its own range
avoid: Weights far above 1 unless the LoRA's page asks for it

images.caption: No LoRA
images.prompt: A lighthouse on a rocky coast at sunset, waves breaking, a few seagulls

images.caption: Weight 0.5
images.prompt: Pixel Art style., A lighthouse on a rocky coast at sunset, waves breaking, a few seagulls

images.caption: Weight 1.0
images.prompt: Pixel Art style., A lighthouse on a rocky coast at sunset, waves breaking, a few seagulls

images.caption: Weight 1.5

tips.title: Lower weights when stacking
tips.body: LoRA effects add up. With two or three LoRAs, reduce each one (often to about 0.4-0.7) so they do not overpower the base model or each other. More than three at high weight usually breaks coherence.
do: Combine one style LoRA with one character or concept LoRA

tips.title: Style vs character vs concept
tips.body: Style LoRAs change the whole look and can often run lower. Character LoRAs need enough weight to hold identity but may lock in pose or clothing from their training images. Concept LoRAs (an object or effect) are often the most sensitive to weight. A common mix: a watercolor style LoRA at 0.6 with a product LoRA at 0.8.

tips.title: Recognize an overcooked LoRA
tips.body: Typical signs: burnt or oversaturated colors, repeated textures, every face looking the same, warped anatomy, or the prompt being ignored. Lower the weight first, then disable LoRAs one at a time to find the culprit.

groups.title: Popular helpers and LoRAs
groups.intro: General notes on widely used add-ons; always check each one's page for exact settings.

tips.title: Turbo, Lightning and Hyper LoRAs
tips.body: Speed LoRAs let a full model run in a handful of steps. Use the step count, CFG (usually around 1) and scheduler they specify; at CFG 1 negative prompts stop working.

tips.title: Detail and skin enhancer LoRAs
tips.body: Detail or realistic-skin LoRAs add texture and micro-detail. They are usually run at low to moderate weight, and some also accept negative weights to reduce detail; too much gives grainy, over-sharpened skin.

images.caption: Without the LoRA
images.prompt: close-up portrait of a middle-aged fisherman on a pier, natural light, photo

images.caption: Flux Skin Detailer at 0.7
images.prompt: close-up portrait of a middle-aged fisherman on a pier, natural light, photo

tips.title: Face and hand detailers
tips.body: Automatic detailers find faces or hands, mask them and inpaint them at higher resolution. Moderate strength (roughly 0.3-0.5) keeps identity and lighting consistent. In VulKara, paint over the face or hand on the Inpaint page and describe just that part.

tips.title: Negative embeddings are model-specific
tips.body: Negative embeddings trained for SD 1.5 only help SD 1.5; SDXL needs its own, and newer transformer models do not use them.

tips.title: Check the model page first
tips.body: Popular checkpoints and LoRAs usually list their recommended sampler, steps, CFG, resolution, VAE and trigger words. Those settings beat general defaults.

tips.title: Expand short ideas for long-prompt models
tips.body: Models with language encoders (Qwen-Image, Z-Image, Krea 2, Wan, Ideogram 4) benefit from turning a short idea into a detailed paragraph, by hand or with a language model.

images.prompt: a woman at night

images.caption: Expanded into a paragraph
images.prompt: A street portrait of a woman in her thirties with short black hair and a yellow raincoat, standing under a neon pharmacy sign at night, wet pavement reflections, eye-level 50mm shot

groups.title: Stable Diffusion 1.5
groups.intro: The classic 512 px family, best with keyword prompts and negative prompts.

tips.title: Write keyword-style prompts
tips.body: SD 1.5 uses a CLIP text encoder that reads about 75 tokens at a time, so short comma-separated keywords work better than long sentences. Put the subject and key style words first.
tips.example: portrait of an old sailor, oil painting, dramatic lighting, rich colors, detailed

images.caption: Plain prompt
images.prompt: an old sailor

images.caption: Keywords, with a negative prompt
images.prompt: portrait of an old sailor, oil painting, dramatic lighting, rich colors, detailed

tips.title: Generate at 512-768 px
tips.body: Base SD 1.5 was trained at 512x512; many finetunes handle up to about 768 px on one side. Larger sizes often duplicate heads or limbs, so upscale afterwards instead.
do: 512x768 or 768x512 for portrait or landscape

tips.title: Rely on negative prompts
tips.body: SD 1.5 benefits clearly from a short negative prompt listing common flaws.
tips.example: Negative: lowres, blurry, bad anatomy, extra fingers, watermark, text

tips.title: Use negative embeddings
tips.body: Textual-inversion embeddings compress a long list of unwanted traits into one token that goes in the negative prompt. Those trained for SD 1.5 do not transfer to SDXL or newer models.
avoid: Using SD 1.5 embeddings with SDXL

tips.title: Typical settings
tips.body: Usually 20-30 steps with guidance around 7 (often 5-9). Community checkpoints often list their preferred sampler, CFG and VAE on their page.

groups.title: SDXL, Pony, Illustrious, NoobAI
groups.intro: 1024 px models; base SDXL takes mixed prompts while anime finetunes expect tags.

tips.title: Stay near 1 megapixel
tips.body: SDXL was trained around 1024x1024. Good alternatives are 1152x896, 1216x832 and 1344x768 and their portrait versions. Small sizes like 512 px look noticeably worse.
do: Pick a size with roughly 1 MP in total

images.caption: 512 px
images.prompt: a knight in armor standing in a castle courtyard at sunset, photo

images.caption: 1024 px
images.prompt: a knight in armor standing in a castle courtyard at sunset, photo

tips.title: Base SDXL settings
tips.body: Usually about 25-40 steps with guidance around 5-8, and negative prompts help. Base SDXL is weak at legible text and complex spatial layouts, so keep scenes simple or fix details by inpainting.

tips.title: Pony: start with score tags
tips.body: Pony Diffusion V6 XL was trained with quality score tags, so prompts usually begin with score_9, score_8_up, score_7_up followed by booru-style tags. Its page also recommends CLIP skip 2 and around 25 steps.
tips.example: score_9, score_8_up, score_7_up, 1boy, adult, knight, armor, castle courtyard, sunset
avoid: Forgetting CLIP skip 2 (gives low-quality blobs)

tips.title: Illustrious and NoobAI: quality + booru tags
tips.body: These anime SDXL finetunes respond to Danbooru-style tags led by quality tags such as masterpiece, best quality. Illustrious usually works with guidance around 4.5-7; the v-prediction NoobAI versions prefer lower guidance (about 3.5-5) to avoid oversaturation.
tips.example: masterpiece, best quality, 1girl, adult, silver hair, long coat, rainy city street, night, neon

tips.title: Use tags the model knows
tips.body: Booru-trained models understand standard Danbooru tag names (looking at viewer, upper body, from side). Invented phrasing is often ignored, so check tag spelling.
do: Put count and subject tags early (1girl, 1boy, solo)

tips.title: Speed up with Lightning or Hyper LoRAs
tips.body: Distillation LoRAs such as SDXL-Lightning or Hyper-SD let SDXL run in about 4-8 steps. Most need very low CFG (around 1, or the value the LoRA states) and a matching scheduler; follow the LoRA's notes.
avoid: Normal CFG 7 with a 4-step LoRA

groups.title: Stable Diffusion 3.5
groups.intro: MMDiT models with three text encoders, good prompt understanding and basic typography.

tips.title: Write natural sentences
tips.body: SD 3.5 combines CLIP with a T5 encoder, so descriptive sentences work better than tag lists. Include style, composition and lighting in plain language.

images.caption: Tag list
images.prompt: cabin, forest, winter, night, lantern, snow

images.caption: Sentences
images.prompt: A small wooden cabin in a snowy pine forest at night, a single lantern glowing by the door, soft snowfall, moonlight through the trees, cinematic wide shot

tips.title: Large: about 28 steps, guidance 3.5-4.5
tips.body: SD 3.5 Large usually runs with about 28 steps and guidance 3.5-4.5. Higher guidance quickly looks harsh.

tips.title: Large Turbo: 4 steps, no guidance
tips.body: The Turbo variant is distilled for about 4 steps with guidance 0, so negative prompts have no effect there.

tips.title: Negative prompts are supported
tips.body: With the non-turbo models, short targeted negative prompts can remove unwanted elements.

tips.title: Stay around 1 megapixel
tips.body: Use about 1024x1024 or an equivalent aspect ratio for the best results.

tips.title: Keep text short
tips.body: SD 3.5 can render short quoted words, but it is less reliable than FLUX, Qwen-Image or Ideogram for longer text.

groups.title: FLUX.1 [dev] and [schnell]
groups.intro: Black Forest Labs' 12B models that follow natural-language prompts closely.

tips.title: Describe the scene in prose
tips.body: FLUX uses a T5 language encoder and follows full sentences well. Write a clear description of subject, setting, light and style; tag lists and weights add little.
tips.example: A cozy bookshop at dusk seen through a rain-streaked window, warm lamps inside, a cat asleep on a stack of novels, soft cinematic light

images.caption: Two words
images.prompt: a bookshop

images.caption: Prose
images.prompt: A cozy bookshop at dusk seen through a rain-streaked window, warm lamps inside, a cat asleep on a stack of novels, soft cinematic light

tips.title: No negative prompt
tips.body: FLUX.1 [dev] and [schnell] are guidance-distilled and ignore negative prompts. Phrase what you want instead, for example sharp focus rather than no blur.

tips.title: [dev]: guidance about 3.5
tips.body: Guidance 3.5 with up to 50 steps is the usual setting; about 20-30 steps is a common faster choice. Slightly lower guidance (about 2-3) often looks more natural for photos, higher follows the prompt more strictly.

tips.title: [schnell]: 1-4 steps, no guidance
tips.body: Schnell is distilled for 1-4 steps with guidance 0, and extra steps rarely help. Its prompt length limit (256 tokens) is shorter than that of [dev].

tips.title: Good at short text
tips.body: Put text in quotes and say where it appears. Short phrases render reliably; long paragraphs do not.

tips.title: Use FLUX.1 LoRAs only
tips.body: LoRAs made for FLUX.1 do not work on FLUX.2 or other families, and SDXL LoRAs never work on FLUX.

groups.title: FLUX.2 [klein]
groups.intro: Compact FLUX.2 models (4B and 9B) for fast generation and editing.

tips.title: Distilled vs base variants
tips.body: The distilled klein models run in about 4 steps with guidance around 1. The klein Base models are undistilled and need about 50 steps with guidance around 4, but are more flexible and meant for fine-tuning.

tips.title: Lead with the most important element
tips.body: Order the prompt as subject, action, style, context: earlier words get more attention. Medium-length prompts of roughly 30-80 words suit most images.
tips.example: A red vintage scooter parked outside a pastel bakery in Lisbon, morning sun, shot on 35mm film, shallow depth of field

tips.title: Describe positively
tips.body: FLUX.2 does not use negative prompts, so describe what you want instead of listing what to avoid.

tips.title: Use hex colors and quoted text
tips.body: FLUX.2 can follow hex color codes tied to an object (walls in #C4725A) and renders quoted text better when you state placement, size and style.

images.caption: Plain prompt
images.prompt: a cafe wall with a sign

images.caption: Hex color and quoted text
images.prompt: A café wall painted in #C4725A with a hanging wooden sign that reads "MORNING" in large white serif letters, centred above the door, soft morning light

tips.title: Editing needs more steps
tips.body: Image to image and reference edits with the distilled models usually need more steps than plain text-to-image; at 4 steps the source can come back almost unchanged.

tips.title: Use FLUX.2 klein LoRAs
tips.body: LoRAs trained for klein usually work best on the distilled checkpoint; FLUX.1 LoRAs are not compatible.

groups.title: Chroma and Chroma1-Flash
groups.intro: An 8.9B open model derived from FLUX.1 [schnell] that keeps real CFG and negative prompts.

tips.title: Real CFG and negatives
tips.body: Unlike FLUX.1, Chroma1-HD runs with true classifier-free guidance, so negative prompts work. About 40 steps with guidance around 3 is a good start.
tips.example: Negative: low quality, blurry, out of focus, unfinished

tips.title: Natural-language prompts
tips.body: Chroma reads prompts with a T5 encoder like FLUX, so descriptive sentences work, and it is flexible across photo and illustration styles.

images.caption: Short prompt
images.prompt: a red fox in a forest

images.caption: Natural language
images.prompt: A red fox standing on a mossy log in a misty birch forest at dawn, golden backlight through the fog, shallow depth of field, wildlife photograph

tips.title: Chroma1-Flash: few steps, CFG about 1
tips.body: Flash has guidance baked in. Usually about 8 steps with a second-order sampler such as Heun, or about 16 steps with other samplers, at CFG around 1-1.5. At CFG 1 negative prompts have no effect. In VulKara it was tested with 12 steps and guidance 1: about 7 minutes per picture at 1024 px on an M2 with 24 GB.

tips.title: Built as a fine-tuning base
tips.body: Chroma1-HD is meant as a starting point for fine-tunes, so community finetunes and Chroma LoRAs may give more polished results for a specific style.

tips.title: Keep prompts clearly safe
tips.body: Chroma's training data is broader and less filtered than many models; write clear prompts and keep the app's content protection on.

groups.title: Qwen-Image and Qwen-Image 2.1
groups.intro: Alibaba's models with strong prompt understanding and the best open rendering of long text.

tips.title: Write long, detailed descriptions
tips.body: Qwen-Image reads prompts with a large vision-language model and handles long, structured prompts with several objects and relations well. Describe layout, colors and text explicitly.

tips.title: Text and posters are its strength
tips.body: It renders multi-line text in English and Chinese, including posters and infographics. Put each piece of text in quotes and say where it goes.
tips.example: A minimalist concert poster: large title "NIGHT TRAIN" at the top in bold white sans-serif, smaller line "Live at the Harbor Hall" below, deep blue background with a single orange train light

images.caption: Plain prompt
images.prompt: a concert poster

images.caption: Text in quotes with its place
images.prompt: A minimalist concert poster: large title "NIGHT TRAIN" at the top in bold white sans-serif, smaller line "Live at the Harbor Hall" below, deep blue background with a single orange train light

tips.title: Original Qwen-Image settings
tips.body: Usually about 50 steps with true CFG around 4. A negative prompt is supported; leaving it empty is fine when nothing needs removing.

tips.title: Use its native aspect ratios
tips.body: Qwen-Image was trained at about 1.3-1.6 MP sizes such as 1328x1328 (1:1), 1664x928 (16:9) and 1472x1140 (4:3). Staying near these sizes gives the cleanest results.

tips.title: Qwen-Image 2.1: smaller, 2K, transparency
tips.body: Version 2.1 is a smaller 7B model with native 2K output, multi-image editing and real transparency: asking for a transparent background can produce an RGBA image. Its license is research and non-commercial only.

tips.title: A short quality suffix can help
tips.body: A brief quality phrase at the end (ultra HD, cinematic composition) can help. It is worth trying, but describing the actual scene matters more.

groups.title: Z-Image Turbo and Base
groups.intro: Tongyi-MAI's 6B models: Turbo for fast results, Base for full control.

tips.title: Turbo: about 9 steps, guidance 0
tips.body: 9 steps (about 8 effective) with guidance 0. Raising guidance or steps far beyond that does not help. In VulKara this takes about 5½ minutes at 1024 px on an M2 with 24 GB (MLX).

tips.title: Turbo ignores negative prompts
tips.body: Because Turbo runs without guidance, write everything positively: describe a clean background instead of listing clutter to avoid.

tips.title: Long natural-language prompts
tips.body: Z-Image uses a Qwen3 language encoder and works best with detailed sentences rather than tag lists. Expanding a short idea into a full paragraph usually improves results.
tips.example: A street portrait of a woman in her thirties with short black hair and a yellow raincoat, standing under a neon pharmacy sign at night, wet pavement reflections, eye-level 50mm shot

images.caption: Short idea
images.prompt: a woman at night

images.caption: Full paragraph
images.prompt: A street portrait of a woman in her thirties with short black hair and a yellow raincoat, standing under a neon pharmacy sign at night, wet pavement reflections, eye-level 50mm shot

tips.title: Quoted text in English or Chinese
tips.body: Z-Image renders bilingual text unusually well for a fast model; put the exact words in quotes.

tips.title: Base: more steps, real CFG
tips.body: Z-Image Base is undistilled. Usually about 28-50 steps with guidance around 3-5, and it responds strongly to negative prompts. Use it when you need negatives, more variety or a base for LoRA training.

tips.title: Leans photorealistic
tips.body: Both versions default toward realistic photos; name an explicit style (illustration, watercolor, 3D render) when you want something else.

groups.title: Krea 2
groups.intro: Krea's open 12B aesthetics-focused model with Turbo and RAW checkpoints.

tips.title: Turbo for images, RAW for training
tips.body: Krea 2 Turbo is an 8-step distilled checkpoint for final images. RAW is the undistilled base meant for fine-tuning and LoRA training; LoRAs trained on RAW are designed to run on Turbo.

tips.title: Natural language with art direction
tips.body: Krea recommends natural-language prompts: long, detailed prompts give the most control, though short ones still look good. Name mood, lighting and visual style clearly.
tips.example: Editorial fashion photo of a man in a rust-colored linen suit on a sun-bleached rooftop, hard midday shadows, desaturated warm palette

images.caption: Short prompt
images.prompt: a man in a suit

images.caption: With art direction
images.prompt: Editorial fashion photo of a man in a rust-colored linen suit on a sun-bleached rooftop, hard midday shadows, desaturated warm palette

tips.title: Keep weights close to 1
tips.body: Its Qwen3-VL encoder reads the prompt as language, so token weights shift the whole prompt; stay at or below about 1.2. Rephrasing works better than heavy weighting.

tips.title: Use Krea 2 LoRAs only
tips.body: Krea 2 was trained from scratch rather than on FLUX or SDXL, so only LoRAs made for Krea 2 are compatible.

groups.title: Ideogram 4
groups.intro: Ideogram's open 9.3B model built for design, layout and typography.

tips.title: Structured JSON captions work best
tips.body: Ideogram 4 was trained on structured JSON captions: a short high-level description, a style block (medium, lighting, color palette) and a list of elements. Plain text also works when it is expanded into that structure first.

tips.title: Quote text and describe its look
tips.body: Give the exact string, keep it short, describe the typographic style (for example condensed bold sans-serif) rather than a font name, and state placement and hierarchy.
tips.example: A kraft-paper coffee bag, product photo, with the headline "FRESH ROAST" in bold black serif letters and the small line "since 1998" beneath it

images.caption: Plain prompt
images.prompt: a coffee bag

images.caption: Quoted text with its look and place
images.prompt: A kraft-paper coffee bag, product photo, with the headline "FRESH ROAST" in bold black serif letters and the small line "since 1998" beneath it

tips.title: Control color and layout
tips.body: Ideogram 4 accepts hex color palettes and bounding boxes for elements, so logos, headings and objects can be placed precisely.

tips.title: Pick the right step preset
tips.body: The reference code offers presets of about 12 steps for drafts, 20 for everyday work and 48 for final images with small type.

tips.title: Flexible sizes up to 2K
tips.body: It supports sizes from 256 to 2048 px in multiples of 16 and very wide aspect ratios, which suits banners and posters. The weights use a non-commercial license.

groups.title: Wan 2.2 video
groups.intro: Open video models where the prompt must describe motion and camera, not just a still scene.

tips.title: Describe motion over time
tips.body: Say what moves and how: who walks where, what the wind does, how the light changes. A still-image prompt tends to give a nearly static clip.
tips.example: A woman in a long coat walks slowly toward the camera along a foggy pier, her scarf moving in the wind, gulls passing overhead

images.caption: Motion and camera: first, middle and last frame of the five-second clip
images.prompt: the lighthouse beam sweeps slowly across the dusk sky, waves roll onto the rocks, slow push-in

tips.title: Use cinematography terms for the camera
tips.body: Wan 2.2 follows common camera language: static shot, pan left, tilt up, dolly in, tracking shot, orbit, crane up.
do: One clear camera move per clip
Start with what the camera sees first
avoid: Several conflicting camera moves in five seconds

tips.title: Short clips at standard sizes
tips.body: The 14B models make about 5-second clips at 480p or 720p (81 frames at 16 fps by default); the 5B TI2V model targets 720p at 24 fps.

tips.title: Negative prompts help
tips.body: Wan runs with real guidance (diffusers defaults: about 50 steps, guidance around 5), so a negative prompt against blur, static frames, flicker and deformed hands is useful.

tips.title: Image-to-video keeps your composition
tips.body: Starting from an image fixes the look and framing; the prompt then only needs to describe motion and camera. The output follows the input image's aspect ratio.

tips.title: Speed LoRAs trade quality for time
tips.body: Distillation LoRAs such as LightX2V cut generation to a few steps with guidance about 1, which disables negative prompts and can reduce motion; good for drafts.

groups.title: ERNIE-Image Turbo
groups.intro: Baidu's 8-step model (Apache 2.0) with dense text rendering, posters and layouts, and its own prompt enhancer.

tips.title: 8 steps, guidance 1
tips.body: ERNIE-Image Turbo is distilled for 8 inference steps with guidance 1.0 (the card's values); more steps or higher guidance do not help, and a negative prompt has no effect. In VulKara it runs on the MLX runtime in 4 bit.
do: Keep the model's 8 steps and guidance 1
avoid: Negative prompts: they are ignored without guidance

tips.title: Write a full caption, or let the enhancer write it
tips.body: The card's example prompt is a long paragraph: camera angle, composition, lighting and color palette. Short prompts work, but the option Prompt enhancer rewrites them into such a caption first (Baidu's own enhancer model, 7.7 GB, downloaded once). It writes the caption in English; the same prompt and seed give the same caption and picture, and the caption is kept as the picture's note.
tips.example: a lighthouse on a rocky coast at dusk
do: Turn on Prompt enhancer for a short idea
Write the paragraph yourself when the layout must stay exactly as you say
avoid: Expecting a different caption from the same prompt and seed

images.caption: Short prompt as written
images.prompt: a lighthouse on a rocky coast at dusk

images.caption: The same prompt and seed, caption written by the enhancer
images.prompt: a lighthouse on a rocky coast at dusk

tips.title: Dense text, posters and panels
tips.body: The model is built for long and layout-sensitive text: posters, infographics, UI-like pictures, comics and multi-panel layouts. Put each piece of text in quotes and say where it goes and how it looks; its weakest benchmark scores are attribute binding and position, so state which object gets which color or place.
tips.example: A travel poster of a mountain lake: the title "ALPENSEE" in large serif letters at the top, a line "open all year" in small caps at the bottom, teal water, a red cabin on the left shore
do: Quote the exact words and name their place and style
avoid: Several objects with swapped colors or places in one sentence

tips.title: Its own sizes
tips.body: The card lists 1024x1024, 848x1264, 1264x848, 768x1376, 896x1200, 1376x768 and 1200x896. Sizes near these give the cleanest pictures; a smaller size is fine for drafts.
do: Pick a size from the card's list for the final picture

tips.title: Memory on a 16 GB Mac
tips.body: The 4 bit model needs about 9 GB; the enhancer about 7 GB more. On a Mac with 16 GB the app unloads the image model before the enhancer runs and loads it again after, so a picture with the enhancer takes about a minute longer.
do: Close other programs before a picture with the enhancer on 16 GB

groups.title: MOSS-Image
groups.intro: OpenMOSS's 5B model (Apache 2.0) for text in pictures, posters and layouts; the 8-step DMD version for speed.

tips.title: 50 steps with CFG 3, or 8 steps with the DMD version
tips.body: The maker's settings are 50 steps, CFG 3 and shift 5 with an Euler sampler; CFG 3 to 6, higher for short prompts. The community 8-step DMD distillation (MOSS-Image 8-step in the Models list) runs in 8 steps without guidance: about 4.5 minutes instead of 40 at 1024 px on an M2 with 24 GB. Its negative prompt has no effect.
do: Draft with the 8-step version, finish with 50 steps when a picture matters
avoid: A negative prompt with the 8-step version

tips.title: Natural language, tags or a layout
tips.body: MOSS-Image reads natural language, tag lists and JSON layouts, up to about 4K tokens. English has the most training data; Chinese and other languages work too. For tags the maker's order is quality, score, meta, year, character, series, artist, general.
tips.example: A cozy bookshop window at dusk, a hand-painted wooden sign above the door reading "VulKara Books", warm light, rain on the glass, photograph
do: Write in English where you can
Put the exact text in quotes

tips.title: Line breaks in text
tips.body: For text with several lines, write the line breaks into the prompt (a real line break or \n) so the model breaks the lines where you want.
tips.example: A chalkboard menu that reads "SOUP OF THE DAY\nTOMATO BASIL\n6 EUR" in white hand lettering

tips.title: A layout as the prompt
tips.body: Paste the JSON of ComfyUI's layout node (or MOSS's Prompt Enhancer skill) as the prompt: a summary caption and items with a label, caption, text and a bbox [top, left, bottom, right] in pixels from the centre of the picture (bbox_coord_space abs_centralized, bbox_format yxyx). The picture's size must match the layout's canvas. Text and objects land where the boxes say.
tips.example: {"summary":{"caption":"A poster for a bakery, warm morning light, a round loaf of bread on a wooden board, clean typography"},"items":[{"label":"text","caption":"headline in bold serif letters","text":"FRESH BREAD","bbox":[-340,-300,-220,300]},{"label":"object","caption":"a round loaf of sourdough bread on a wooden board","bbox":[-150,-250,250,250]},{"label":"text","caption":"small caption line","text":"baked every morning","bbox":[300,-200,360,200]}],"bbox_coord_space":"abs_centralized","bbox_format":"yxyx"}
do: Set the picture size to the layout's canvas (768 px here)
avoid: Boxes that overlap or leave the canvas

images.caption: The same poster described in words
images.prompt: A poster for a bakery, warm morning light, a round loaf of sourdough bread on a wooden board, the headline "FRESH BREAD" in bold serif letters at the top and the small caption "baked every morning" at the bottom, clean typography

images.caption: The layout JSON as the prompt
images.prompt: {"summary":{"caption":"A poster for a bakery, warm morning light, a round loaf of bread on a wooden board, clean typography"},"items":[{"label":"text","caption":"headline in bold serif letters","text":"FRESH BREAD","bbox":[-340,-300,-220,300]},{"label":"object","caption":"a round loaf of sourdough bread on a wooden board","bbox":[-150,-250,250,250]},{"label":"text","caption":"small caption line","text":"baked every morning","bbox":[300,-200,360,200]}],"bbox_coord_space":"abs_centralized","bbox_format":"yxyx"}

tips.title: Stripes in flat areas: the Destripe LoRA
tips.body: The SFT model often paints evenly spaced vertical color stripes across smooth areas (skies, fog, walls, backdrops). nynxz's Destripe LoRA, extracted from the model rather than trained, takes them out: strength 1 at 768 px, 1.5 at 1024 px, on the SFT model and the 8-step version only, not on Base.
do: Import the Destripe LoRA for posters and flat colors
avoid: Strength 2: no better than 1.5

tips.title: Sizes and memory
tips.body: The model makes 1 to 2 megapixels and takes sizes from 512 px up to 2K in multiples of 16, any aspect ratio. In VulKara the transformer runs in 8 bit and the text encoder in 4 bit: about 9 GB, so it fits a 16 GB Mac.

groups.title: Fibo 2.0 Edit Turbo and Dev
groups.intro: Bria AI's 8B models (CC BY-NC 4.0): Edit Turbo edits by instruction in 4 steps, Dev paints from text in 50.

tips.title: Edit Turbo: 4 steps, guidance 1
tips.body: Edit Turbo is distilled: 4 steps with guidance 1.0 (the card's values) and no negative prompt. Fibo 2.0 Dev is the undistilled base: 50 steps with guidance 5.0, two passes per step, about an hour per picture at 1024 px on an M2 with 24 GB. In VulKara, Edit Turbo runs on ComfyUI from 20 GB and on MLX in 8 bit on 16 GB Macs.
do: Edit Turbo for edits and quick pictures, Dev when the prompt must be followed closely
avoid: A negative prompt with Edit Turbo

tips.title: Edit by a plain instruction
tips.body: Give the start picture and say what should change, as to a person: replace, add, remove, make it. The model keeps identity, layout, lighting and the parts you did not mention. The whole picture is repainted, so small drifts are normal; use a mask when nothing else may move.
tips.example: Make it a snowy winter night with a full moon
do: One change per instruction
Name what to keep when it matters: keep the face and the pose

images.caption: Start picture
images.prompt: a lighthouse on a rocky coast at dusk

images.caption: Edited by instruction (MLX, 8 bit, 4 steps)
images.prompt: Make it a snowy winter night with a full moon

tips.title: Masked edits keep the rest pixel for pixel
tips.body: With a mask (Inpainting, AI Canvas) only the white part is repainted and everything else is copied from the original. Describe the whole area under the mask, not only the new object.
tips.example: the white base of the lighthouse tower with a small red wooden cabin beside it

tips.title: Up to four pictures in one edit
tips.body: Image to image takes up to three more pictures under More pictures. Refer to them in order as <image_1> (the start picture), <image_2> and so on. Each further picture costs memory (about 2.2 GB on ComfyUI, 0.5 GB on MLX) and time: with four pictures a step takes 3.5 to 4 times as long.
tips.example: Put the lighthouse from <image_1> as a small framed painting in the shop window of <image_2>
avoid: Expecting every picture to be used: the model may keep the sign of <image_2> instead of taking the one from <image_3>

tips.title: Text to image: describe like a caption
tips.body: Fibo 2.0 was trained on structured captions (Bria's VGL JSON: objects with counts, positions and attributes, a style block). A plain prompt works; the closer it reads to such a caption, the more precisely counts, places and colors are followed. Short quoted text renders well.
tips.example: A cozy bookshop window at dusk, a hand-painted wooden sign above the door reading "VulKara Books", warm light, rain on the glass, photograph

tips.title: Sizes
tips.body: About one megapixel in multiples of 16: 1024x1024, 1424x800 or 1248x832 (the card's examples). An edit at a smaller size rebuilds the picture more than at 1024 px: edit at 1024 px when the start picture should stay recognisable.
do: Edit at 1024 px
avoid: Edits at 512 px: the scene changes more than asked

tips.title: LoRAs on both runtimes
tips.body: LoRAs trained for Fibo 2.0 work on ComfyUI and on MLX: VulKara converts between the two layouts at import. Start around strength 0.9 and use the trigger word; a LoRA trained with a few hundred steps changes the composition more than the style.

groups.title: FLUX 3 Image Klein
groups.intro: Black Forest Labs' distilled model with its own prompt upsampler, edits from reference pictures and layouts by boxes; on Macs in 6 or 8 bit on the MLX runtime (FLUX Kommunity License, non-commercial).

tips.title: 16 steps without guidance
tips.body: The distilled Klein samples 16 steps with no guidance (the maker's values); at 4 steps the picture comes out under-denoised and grainy. Klein Base is the undistilled version: 50 steps with guidance (3.5 to 4 in the maker's examples). About 7 s per step at 1024 px on an M4 Pro in 6 bit; draft at a smaller size and render the final picture larger, up to 4K.
do: Keep the 16 steps
Draft small, render the final picture at full size
avoid: Fewer steps to save time: grain instead of detail

tips.title: Let the upsampler write the caption
tips.body: The model was trained on captions its own upsampler writes, so a short prompt as typed gives a generic picture; the maker says not to use the model without it. The option Prompt upsampler turns a short idea into the full caption (a vision-language model, about 10-20 s more) and keeps it as the picture's note. Writing the caption yourself works too: framing first, then the subject with its action, colors and materials, the background, the lighting, and a short style line with medium, lens and palette.
tips.example: a double exposure of a wolf and a pine forest
do: Turn on Prompt upsampler for a short prompt
Framing first when you write the caption yourself
avoid: A product label left unnamed: the model invents text for it

images.caption: As typed
images.prompt: a double exposure of a wolf and a pine forest

images.caption: With the prompt upsampler
images.prompt: a double exposure of a wolf and a pine forest

tips.title: Edits from a reference picture
tips.body: The model edits from up to ten reference pictures and refers to them by position (the second image); the first reference sets the output size. In VulKara the start picture of Image to image is the reference. The upsampler is for text to image: an edit uses the instruction as written.
do: Say what should change, as to a person

tips.title: The same seed holds the layout
tips.body: The same prompt and seed give the same picture. Keep the seed and change one clause at a time to try lighting or style while the composition stays largely intact; a strong anchor rather than a lock, larger changes move more of the scene.
do: Change one clause at a time with the seed fixed

tips.title: Hands, faces and text
tips.body: The maker of the Mac conversion notes occasional hand and finger errors and a smooth, slightly waxy skin on some portraits; text rendering can be inaccurate. Detailed prompts, the upsampler and another seed help.
avoid: Long text in the picture

groups.title: Anima
groups.intro: CircleStone Labs' and Comfy Org's 2B anime model in the versions Base, Aesthetic and Turbo, with community fine-tunes for other looks; on ComfyUI. Non-commercial licence, the pictures may be used commercially.

tips.title: Turbo: 8-12 steps, CFG 1
tips.body: Anima-Turbo is distilled: CFG 1 and 8-12 steps, only slightly behind Aesthetic on average but less varied; VulKara sets 10 steps and CFG 1 for a Turbo checkpoint. Base and Aesthetic take 30-50 steps with CFG 4-5. The maker's sampler is er_sde; euler a gives softer, thinner lines, euler suits Turbo and Aesthetic.
do: Draft on Turbo, finish on Aesthetic or a fine-tune
avoid: CFG above 1 on Turbo

tips.title: Danbooru tags, lowercase with spaces
tips.body: Trained on Danbooru tags, natural language and mixtures of both. Write tags lowercase with spaces, not underscores (score tags excepted); where Danbooru and Gelbooru differ, the Gelbooru form. The maker's prefix is masterpiece, best quality, score_7, safe, with a negative prompt of worst quality, low quality, blurry, jpeg artifacts; with the Aesthetic version quality tags are optional and score tags stay out of both prompts. Order: quality, meta, year and safety, then subject count, character, series, artist, general tags.
tips.example: masterpiece, best quality, score_7, safe, 1girl, cat ears, silver hair, blue eyes, school uniform, standing by a window, holding a cup of tea, rain outside the window, warm lamp light, soft shading, detailed background
do: Lowercase tags with spaces
The safety tag in every prompt
avoid: Underscores in tags
Score tags with the Aesthetic version

images.caption: Three tags
images.prompt: 1girl, cat ears, safe

images.caption: Quality prefix, subject, scene and light
images.prompt: masterpiece, best quality, score_7, safe, 1girl, cat ears, silver hair, blue eyes, school uniform, standing by a window, holding a cup of tea, rain outside the window, warm lamp light, soft shading, detailed background

tips.title: Artists with @, weights higher than on SDXL
tips.body: An artist's name takes an @ in front; without it the effect is very weak. Weighting works but needs higher values than SDXL: the maker's example is (chibi:2).
tips.example: @artist name, 1girl, (chibi:2), simple background

tips.title: Natural language: at least two sentences
tips.body: Very short prompts give unexpected pictures; write at least two sentences, and with several characters describe each one's look. Short or vague prompts can also bring unwanted content: the safety tag and detail help.
do: Describe every character when there are several
avoid: One vague line

tips.title: Anime, not realism or long text
tips.body: Anima is weak at realism by design (realistic fine-tunes such as realistic-skin versions push it there) and poor at longer text; single words and short phrases render better.
avoid: A paragraph of text in the picture

groups.title: Lumina 2, Neta Lumina and NetaYume
groups.intro: Alpha-VLLM's 2B Lumina-Image 2.0 (Apache 2.0) and its anime fine-tunes Neta Lumina and NetaYume with a Gemma 2 text encoder; on ComfyUI.

tips.title: 40-50 steps with CFG 4-7
tips.body: NetaYume's card: 40-50 steps, CFG 4-7, the samplers Euler a or res_multistep (Neta Lumina: 30 steps, CFG 4-5.5, scheduler linear_quadratic); Lumina 2's example uses 50 steps with guidance 4. VulKara sets 40 steps, CFG 5.5 and res_multistep for the Neta models and 36 steps with CFG 4 for Lumina 2.
do: 40 steps or more for a finished picture

tips.title: The system prompt comes first
tips.body: The Neta models were trained with a system prompt for anime ("You are an assistant designed to generate anime images based on textual prompts." followed by a prompt start marker). VulKara puts the fitting prefix in front of every prompt for them; you write only the picture.
do: Write only the picture, the prefix is added

tips.title: Danbooru tags or sentences, three languages
tips.body: Tags and natural language both work; Neta Lumina names Chinese, English and Japanese as the first languages. Danbooru-style tags with the quality words first, then the character, then the scene.
tips.example: masterpiece, best quality, 1girl, silver hair, long hair, green eyes, reading a book, sitting, library, bookshelf, warm light, window, detailed background, highres
do: Quality tags first, then character, then scene

images.caption: Three words
images.prompt: a girl reading

images.caption: Danbooru tags with quality words
images.prompt: masterpiece, best quality, 1girl, silver hair, long hair, green eyes, reading a book, sitting, library, bookshelf, warm light, window, detailed background, highres

tips.title: Sizes of about one megapixel
tips.body: Neta Lumina lists 1024 × 1024, 768 × 1532 and 968 × 1322 or larger. On a 16 GB Mac VulKara loads NetaYume in parts (the text encoder and the model apart).
do: Portrait 768 × 1532 for a standing figure

tips.title: The negative prompt works
tips.body: Real guidance, so the negative prompt counts: VulKara's default for the Neta models is blurry, worst quality, low quality, jpeg artifacts, signature, watermark.
tips.example: Negative: blurry, worst quality, low quality, jpeg artifacts, signature, watermark

groups.title: AuraFlow and Pony V7
groups.intro: fal's open 6.8B flow model AuraFlow v0.3 (Apache 2.0) and Pony V7, the character model built on it (Pony License); on Diffusers, Pony V7 as GGUF on ComfyUI.

tips.title: 50 steps with guidance 3.5, up to 1536 px
tips.body: AuraFlow v0.3's example: 50 steps, guidance 3.5, sizes up to 1536 px on a side in various aspect ratios (1536 × 768 in the card). Pony V7 asks for at least 30 steps and 768-1536 px, the higher the better.
tips.example: Astronaut in a jungle, cold color palette, muted colors, detailed, 8k
do: Higher resolution and 30 steps or more on Pony V7

images.caption: Plain prompt
images.prompt: an astronaut in a jungle

images.caption: The card's example: palette, mood and quality words
images.prompt: Astronaut in a jungle, cold color palette, muted colors, detailed, 8k

tips.title: Pony V7: special tags, facts, style, tags
tips.body: The template: special tags (score_X, style_cluster_x, source_X), then a factual description of the picture, then the style (medium, shot type, lighting), then further content tags. Open with one phrase that sums up the picture, then the details; natural language works in most cases, and tags appended at the end emphasize.
tips.example: A lone lighthouse keeper on a stormy cliff at night, digital painting, wide shot, cold rim light
do: One summing-up phrase first, then the details

tips.title: Characters: species, gender, name, source
tips.body: Name a character as species, gender, name and source; the card's example: Anthro bunny female Lola Bunny from Space Jam.
tips.example: Anthro bunny female Lola Bunny from Space Jam

tips.title: Weaker quality tags, no text, small faces
tips.body: On V7 the special and quality tags work much less than on V6 (score_9 does not reliably help), text in the picture is not supported, and small details and faces can degrade with the art style; the makers point to V7.1. Inpaint a face at a larger size when it matters.
avoid: Relying on score_9
Text in the picture
